correctness.rationale: PASS. Reconstructed the singleton-approval reduction with three minority-round frequencies c1>=c2>=c3 and the two explicit switch cases, proving each voter >=floor(d/3) and two voters >=floor(2d/3) on contested rounds. All unanimous rounds add common utility; replacing double approvals with a singleton can only lower a fixed outcome utility. A Pareto completion using O(ell^4) satisfaction-vector DP preserves quota guarantees. Each singleton coalition is blocked by floor(ell/3), each pair by one of the two high-utility voters at floor(2ell/3), and the grand coalition by Pareto efficiency under the exact Section 6 strong-core definition. An independent complete finite full-ballot profile calculation for all 20,439 ordered elections of 1,2,3 rounds verified existence of a Pareto quota-satisfying outcome; universal correctness is the analytic argument.
